summary: Paper 110 advances the theory of near-Monge matrices with sparse negative mixed differences, directly addressing Open Problem 3 and Appendix D of Chen (arXiv:2611.34733v1). First, a greedy 2-approximate vertex cover of the bipartite negative-support graph induces a symmetric cut partition into at most 2*tau(C)+1 intervals whose off-diagonal blocks and diagonal triangles are purely Monge, enabling SMAWK plus Wilber doubling-phase DP with arbitrary base potentials in deterministic O(s + n(tau(C)+1)) time with zero log factors. Second, a four-corner distinct-gap property yields the exact rank sandwich max(ceil(s/2), max_p s_row(p), max_q s_col(q)) <= r_min(C) <= s(C) (tight at both ends) and an (n-2)^2 deterministic / Omega(n^2) randomized entry-oracle lower bound for Monge testing. Third, replacing (j-k)^2 with binomial(j-k,2) compresses Chen hardness weights to Theta(n^{1+alpha}), and an O(r)-node elementary-block envelope tree accelerates static min-plus rectangle updates by Theta(log n / log(r+2)).
strengths: Symmetric vertex-cover cut partition S = {0,n} U {p+1: p in R_cuts} U {q: q in C_cuts} enforces |I_u|=|J_u|, respects sequential prefix dependencies, and eliminates all logarithmic factors in O(s + n(tau(C)+1)) DP time (Theorem 2.3).
Exact four-corner distinct-gap analysis of signed rectangles (Lemma 3.1) separates r_min(C) from ceil(s(C)/2) via row/column gap maxima and achieves exact tightness at both s/2 and s (Theorem 3.2).
Clean (n-2)^2 deterministic and Omega(n^2) randomized entry-oracle lower bound via single interior +5 perturbations on 2(j-k)^2, directly answering Chen Appendix D.

Minimal unit-curvature integer background binomial(j-k,2) and tight multiplier lam_tri = max(2, (a-1)(n-1)+1) yield >8x weight compression for 2 <= a <= n/4 while preserving exact integer ceiling recovery for all V in Z (Theorem 4.2a).

Strong multi-layer verification: 20 constructive Lean 4.35.0 theorems (verified locally with 0 sorry and [propext, Quot.sound] only), 16 AST-audited zero-float SHA-256 certificates, and 56 passing adversarial pytest tests including executable SMAWK and Wilber routines.
weaknesses: The vertex-cover DP speedup requires tau(C) = o(log^3 n) and assumes the negative-support list N_ut(C) and O(1) entry oracle are given; when negative cells form an induced matching of size Theta(n), the bound degrades to O(n^2).

Lean 4.35.0 formalizes the 20 core algebraic, cut-invariance, and combinatorial invariants rather than full imperative runtime complexity or pointer termination of SMAWK, Wilber, and the switch-column envelope tree (which are proved in prose and tested on finite instances).

In Theorem 4.2(b), the static tree bound writes log(r+2) in Eq. (19) (for r >= 1), whereas the proof notes L_r = O(min(log n, log(r+2))); for dense r > n this factor caps at log n and for r=0 the O(n T_M) SMAWK branch applies.
strong_novelty_candidates: Symmetric vertex-cover cut partitioning with Wilber doubling-phase diagonal sweeps over arbitrary base potentials, resolving Chen Open Problem 3 in the vertex-cover regime with zero logarithmic factors.

Exact signed-rectangle rank sandwich max(ceil(s/2), s_row, s_col) <= r_min(C) <= s(C) separating r_min from ceil(s/2) by a factor of 2, paired with an exact (n-2)^2 entry-oracle Monge-testing lower bound.
Unit-curvature triangular background binomial(j-k,2) with tight O(n^{1+alpha}) multiplier compression and O(r)-node elementary-block static envelope tree with monotone leaf fingers.
